newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland invites bids for Ostroleka meat firm.
newsitem.headline: Poland invites bids for Ostroleka meat firm.

text.p: Poland's Treasury Ministry advertised in newspapers on Monday to invite bids for state meat firm Panstwowy Zaklady Miesne Ostroleka SA.

"The Treasury Minister offers the value of the entire capital, reduced by the number of shares which will be granted to employees...suppliers...allocated to funding the social security system or...retained by the treasury for reprivatisation," the advertisement said.
It said bids could be submitted until April 4.
A ministry official earlier said that it would offer no less than 10 percent and no more than 55 percent of Ostroleka's 1,350,000 shares.

Employees would get up to 15 percent, as would farmers cooperating with the company, while up to 10 percent would go to pension funds formed in the restructuring of the country's social security system.
Five percent would go to restitution claims for property taken under the previous communist system, the official said.
Polish meat processor Sokolow SA said last week it was considering buying all the available shares in Ostroleka.

"We sent a letter of intent concerning the purchase of all shares put up for sale by the state treasury, but so far we do not know how many shares that will be," Sokolow's deputy president Krzysztof Lewczuk told Reuters.
Ostroleka, which employs over 1,300 people, made a 3.3 million zloty net loss in 1996 and lost three million zlotys in 1995 on sales of 98.5 million zlotys and 93 million zlotys respectively.
